## UPSC IES ISS 2026: Indian Economic Service and Indian Statistical Service recruitment

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the combined Indian Economic Service (IES) and Indian Statistical Service (ISS) examination once a year to recruit Grade A officers into two of India's most specialised civil services. The IES supplies economics-trained officers to ministries like Finance, Commerce, Planning, and NITI Aayog. The ISS supplies statistically trained officers to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and the Reserve Bank of India. The 2026 notification is expected in September 2026 with the written exam in June or July 2027. Total vacancies typically range from 30 to 60 across both services combined.

This is a niche exam. Fewer than 6,000 candidates appear for both services combined in a typical year. That is roughly the same size as a single UPSC CSE Mains cohort. Selection ratios are far better than UPSC CSE (about 1:150 for IES and 1:100 for ISS versus 1:800 for CSE), while the starting salary and posting quality match Grade A civil service standards.

## Important dates for UPSC IES ISS 2026

| Event | Date (expected) |
|---|---|
| Official notification | September 2026 |
| Registration opens | September 2026 |
| Last date to apply | October 2026 |
| Admit card release | May or June 2027 |
| Written examination | June or July 2027 |
| Written result | September 2027 |
| Personal interview | November or December 2027 |
| Final result | January or February 2028 |

Confirm every date against upsc.gov.in when the official notification is released. Dates above reflect the typical IES/ISS cycle timing from 2023, 2024, and 2025 recruitments.

## IES and ISS: what they are and where officers work

### Indian Economic Service (IES)

IES officers work as economists inside the central government. Typical postings and functions:

- Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Expenditure, Department of Revenue)
- Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce, DPIIT)
- NITI Aayog (policy research and evaluation)
- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (economic analysis wing)
- Reserve Bank of India deputations (occasionally)
- Department of Public Enterprises
- Other ministries needing in-house economic analysis capacity

The role is analytical and advisory. IES officers write policy briefs, evaluate schemes, model economic outcomes, and support senior civil servants and ministers with economic reasoning behind decisions.

### Indian Statistical Service (ISS)

ISS officers work as statisticians across ministries that produce or consume large-scale data. Typical postings:

- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (National Statistical Office, Central Statistics Office)
- National Sample Survey Office
- Registrar General of India (Census Commissioner's office)
- Ministry of Agriculture (agricultural statistics)
- Ministry of Labour (labour bureau and employment statistics)
- Reserve Bank of India deputations
- International Statistical Institute affiliations

The role is technical and data-heavy. ISS officers design surveys, run statistical estimation for national aggregates (GDP, CPI, employment), and increasingly work on modern data-analytics workflows adopted by government departments.

## Vacancies for IES ISS 2026

Vacancy distribution varies by cycle. Using recent years as a reference:

| Year | IES vacancies | ISS vacancies | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 25 | 26 | 51 |
| 2024 | 22 | 26 | 48 |
| 2025 | 20 | 27 | 47 |

Expect 2026 vacancies to fall in the 40 to 60 range. Selection is category-wise as per government reservation rules: UR, EWS, OBC NCL, SC, ST, PwBD.

## Eligibility for UPSC IES ISS 2026

### Age

Age 21 to 30 years as on August 1 of the notification year (August 1, 2026 for the 2026 cycle). Age relaxation applies:

- OBC NCL: up to 33 years
- SC and ST: up to 35 years
- PwBD (UR): up to 40 years
- PwBD (OBC): up to 43 years
- PwBD (SC or ST): up to 45 years
- Ex-servicemen: 5 years additional per rules

### Education

Eligibility is service-specific. A candidate cannot apply for both services in the same year.

For **IES**, a Master's degree in Economics, Applied Economics, Business Economics, or Econometrics from a recognised university is required. Interdisciplinary economics degrees are accepted if the university officially classifies them as Economics degrees.

For **ISS**, a Bachelor's degree with Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, or Applied Statistics as one of the subjects, OR a Master's degree in Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, or Applied Statistics from a recognised university.

Candidates in the final year of qualifying degree can apply provisionally but must submit their degree certificate by the deadline in the notification.

### Nationality

Indian citizens, plus Nepalese and Bhutanese subjects, Tibetan refugees who came to India before January 1, 1962, and persons of Indian origin who migrated from certain listed countries with intent to settle in India. The last two categories need a Government of India eligibility certificate.

## Application fee for UPSC IES ISS 2026

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC, EWS (Male) | Rs. 200 |
| SC, ST, PwBD, Women (all categories) | Nil |

Payment is online via UPI, net banking, debit card, or credit card, or offline via SBI Bank Challan.

## How to apply for UPSC IES ISS 2026 step by step

Applications go through the UPSC One Time Registration (OTR) portal at upsconline.nic.in only.

1. Visit upsconline.nic.in and complete UPSC OTR if not already done. OTR is a one-time process; the same OTR ID works across all UPSC exams.
2. Log in to the OTR portal and open the IES/ISS 2026 examination form.
3. Choose the service (IES or ISS) and fill personal details, qualification details, and centre preferences.
4. Upload photograph, signature, and photo identification (as per size and format specifications in the notification).
5. Pay the fee online or via SBI Bank Challan.
6. Submit and download the confirmation page. Print two copies for records.

The withdrawal window opens for a few days after the last date. If you decide not to appear, use it to save the record.

## UPSC IES ISS 2026 exam pattern

The examination has two stages: a written examination worth 1000 marks and a personal interview worth 200 marks. Total is 1200 marks.

### Written examination (1000 marks, 6 papers over 3 days)

Two papers are common to both services. Four papers are service-specific.

Common papers:

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | General English | 100 | 3 hours |
| II | General Studies | 100 | 3 hours |

Service-specific papers for IES:

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| III | General Economics I | 200 | 3 hours |
| IV | General Economics II | 200 | 3 hours |
| V | General Economics III | 200 | 3 hours |
| VI | Indian Economics | 200 | 3 hours |

Service-specific papers for ISS:

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| III | Statistics I (Objective) | 200 | 2 hours |
| IV | Statistics II (Objective) | 200 | 2 hours |
| V | Statistics III (Descriptive) | 200 | 3 hours |
| VI | Statistics IV (Descriptive) | 200 | 3 hours |

All descriptive papers are in English only. There is no compulsory Indian language paper.

### Personal interview (200 marks)

Candidates who clear the written cutoff are called for a personal interview at UPSC headquarters in Delhi (Dholpur House). The panel typically includes 4 to 5 members. Interview weightage is 200 out of 1200 total marks, roughly 16.7 percent.

Final merit is the sum of written and interview marks.

## Syllabus focus for IES and ISS

### IES syllabus focus areas (Papers III to VI)

Paper III (General Economics I): microeconomics (consumer theory, producer theory, market structures), macroeconomics (national income, IS-LM, monetary and fiscal policy), international trade theory, growth models.

Paper IV (General Economics II): public finance, environmental economics, welfare economics, development economics, monetary theory, banking and finance.

Paper V (General Economics III): quantitative methods (statistics, econometrics), Indian economic history from 1950, industrial economics, labour economics.

Paper VI (Indian Economics): Indian macroeconomic performance since 1991, structural reforms, agricultural policy, industrial policy, poverty and inequality, current five-year and multi-year economic strategies, budget analysis for the last 3 years.

### ISS syllabus focus areas (Papers III to VI)

Paper III (Statistics I, Objective): probability, distributions, statistical inference, hypothesis testing.

Paper IV (Statistics II, Objective): linear models, sampling, design of experiments, statistical computing basics.

Paper V (Statistics III, Descriptive): applied statistics including time series, index numbers, official statistics.

Paper VI (Statistics IV, Descriptive): choice of one specialisation from Operations Research, Econometrics, Sampling Techniques, Demography, Actuarial Statistics, or Statistical Computing.

## Salary and service structure for IES ISS 2026

IES and ISS officers are placed in the Junior Time Scale (Grade A) on joining:

| Component | Approximate value |
|---|---|
| Basic Pay (Level 10, 7th CPC) | Rs. 56,100 per month |
| Dearness Allowance (about 55% of basic) | Rs. 30,855 |
| House Rent Allowance | Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 27,000 (varies by city) |
| Transport Allowance | Rs. 3,600 to Rs. 7,200 |
| Other allowances | Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 5,000 |
| **Gross monthly (Delhi posting)** | **Rs. 1.05 lakh to Rs. 1.20 lakh** |

Net in-hand after NPS, tax, and other deductions is approximately Rs. 80,000 to Rs. 95,000 at Junior Time Scale.

Beyond salary, officers receive:

- Government accommodation in Delhi or the state of posting, at nominal licence fee
- Government vehicle for official duty at Senior Time Scale (Grade B) and above
- Full medical coverage under CGHS for self and family
- Leave Travel Concession every 2 years
- Contribution to NPS
- Study leave and deputation opportunities including international training

Total annual CTC at entry level is approximately Rs. 15 to Rs. 18 lakh including all monetary and non-monetary perks.

## Career progression in IES and ISS

Both services follow the standard central civil service progression:

Junior Time Scale (Grade A) then Senior Time Scale (Grade B), Junior Administrative Grade (Grade C), Selection Grade (Grade D), Senior Administrative Grade (Grade E), Higher Administrative Grade, and finally Apex Scale (Secretary in Government of India).

Typical timing: Junior to Senior Time Scale in 4 years, then approximately 4 to 6 years per subsequent scale. Officers who reach Higher Administrative Grade or Apex Scale can head departments like the National Statistical Office or serve as Chief Economic Adviser in ministries. Compensation at Apex Scale exceeds Rs. 2.5 lakh per month base plus perks.

## Preparation strategy for UPSC IES ISS 2026

### General English (Paper I)

Focus on essay writing, precis, and comprehension. This paper is qualifying-heavy in terms of impact on your ranking because most candidates score in a tight 45 to 55 range. Practice at least 2 essays and 3 precis per week for the last 3 months.

### General Studies (Paper II)

Overlaps significantly with UPSC CSE Prelims General Studies. Any standard CSE Prelims prep material (Manorama Yearbook, Laxmikanth Polity, Bipan Chandra History) is sufficient. Do not over-prepare this paper; focus your best hours on subject papers.

### IES subject papers (III to VI)

The four IES papers are the ranking decider. Standard reference books:

- Microeconomics: Varian, or Snyder and Nicholson
- Macroeconomics: Blanchard, or Mankiw
- Public Finance: Musgrave and Musgrave
- International Trade: Krugman and Obstfeld
- Development Economics: Todaro and Smith
- Indian Economics: Uma Kapila, or the Economic Survey of the last 3 years
- Econometrics: Gujarati

Solve 10 years of previous year papers. UPSC repeats question types and even specific concepts every 4 to 5 years in the IES syllabus.

### ISS subject papers (III to VI)

Statistics-focused prep, with the two objective papers (III, IV) closer in style to CSIR NET Statistics, and the two descriptive papers (V, VI) requiring problem-solving demonstrations.

- Probability and inference: Rohatgi and Saleh, or S.C. Gupta and V.K. Kapoor
- Linear models and sampling: Cochran, or Kish
- Applied statistics: Croxton, Cowden, and Klein
- For Paper VI specialisation: choose based on your comfort. Operations Research (Taha) and Econometrics (Gujarati) are the most-picked electives.

### Interview

The IES/ISS interview panel probes depth in your chosen service's core area far more than UPSC CSE panels do. Prepare for questions like "Explain the current stance of RBI's monetary policy" (IES) or "Design a sampling plan for measuring urban unemployment in Delhi" (ISS). Vague answers do not survive the follow-up.

## UPSC IES ISS vs UPSC CSE: which one to target

Both are Grade A civil service entries. Choose based on your academic strength, career interest, and competition tolerance.

| Feature | UPSC IES / ISS | UPSC CSE |
|---|---|---|
| Selection ratio | 1:100 to 1:150 | 1:800 to 1:1,000 |
| Vacancies (typical) | 40 to 60 combined | 1,000 to 1,100 |
| Written exam total | 1,000 marks | 1,750 marks |
| Number of papers | 6 | 9 (including 4 optional) |
| Interview weightage | ~17 percent | ~15 percent |
| Optional subject choice | Only for ISS Paper VI | Yes, 1 of 26 subjects |
| Qualification required | Master's in Economics or Statistics | Any bachelor's degree |
| Age limit (General) | 30 years | 32 years |
| Attempt limit (General) | 6 | 6 |
| Postings | Ministries and agencies dealing with economics or data | Full spectrum of IAS/IPS/IFS/IRS and 20+ services |
| Entry pay (Level 10) | Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.20 lakh gross | Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.20 lakh gross |
| Suitable if | Master's in Economics or Statistics; interest in analytical or research-heavy roles | Any degree; interest in field administration or policy leadership |

For candidates who already hold a Master's in Economics or Statistics from a strong programme, IES/ISS is often the higher-expected-value path because competition is lower and the ceiling is comparable at Apex Scale.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Attempting IES with only a Bachelor's in Economics. Eligibility for IES requires a Master's; a Bachelor's alone does not qualify.
- Underestimating Paper I (English). Candidates who score 60+ in English gain 5 to 10 ranks on the merit list versus the median.
- Skipping Indian Economics (Paper VI) preparation because it "should come naturally". This paper has the highest year-on-year change in content and needs the last 3 years' Economic Survey memorised.
- For ISS, choosing an unfamiliar Paper VI specialisation. Pick the elective you did in your Master's or one you have prepared for over 6 months.
- Treating the interview as a formality. IES/ISS panels test depth aggressively; a shallow subject knowledge shows quickly.

## Frequently asked questions

**When will the UPSC IES ISS 2026 notification be released?**
The 2026 notification is expected in September 2026, with the written exam in June or July 2027. Confirm dates on upsc.gov.in once the official notification is released.

**Is there negative marking in IES ISS papers?**
Yes, for the two ISS objective papers (Paper III and Paper IV). Descriptive papers do not have negative marking. Common English and General Studies papers do not have negative marking either.

**Can I appear for both IES and ISS in the same year?**
No. Candidates must choose one service (IES or ISS) at the time of application. Applying for both in the same cycle is not allowed.

**What is the salary of an IES or ISS officer at entry level?**
Junior Time Scale (Grade A) officers receive a gross monthly package of Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.20 lakh in Delhi, with net in-hand of Rs. 80,000 to Rs. 95,000 after NPS and tax. Total annual CTC including allowances and perks is Rs. 15 to Rs. 18 lakh.

**Can a Statistics graduate (Bachelor's) apply for ISS?**
Yes, provided your Bachelor's had Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, or Applied Statistics as one of the subjects. Master's in Statistics is not mandatory for ISS eligibility.

**Which is easier, IES or ISS?**
Neither is objectively easier. IES has slightly fewer applicants per vacancy (about 1:100 vs 1:150 for IES vs ISS ratios in recent years). Difficulty depends on your academic background. A candidate with a strong Statistics Master's finds ISS more approachable; a candidate with an Economics Master's finds IES more approachable.

**What is the attempt limit for UPSC IES ISS?**
6 attempts for General category, 9 for OBC NCL, unlimited for SC and ST candidates until the age limit is reached.

**How much time is needed to prepare for IES ISS from scratch?**
For a Master's holder in the relevant subject, 8 to 12 months of dedicated preparation is typical. For candidates fresh from a Bachelor's programme with Statistics coursework, 12 to 18 months is a realistic timeline.

**Is coaching necessary for UPSC IES ISS?**
No. The exam has a small candidate pool and most successful candidates prepare through self-study using standard subject textbooks and previous year papers. Coaching is available in Delhi for IES specifically and is useful for the Indian Economics paper if you are not already engaged with policy content.

**Can IES or ISS officers switch to IAS later?**
Yes, through the Combined Services Examination (CSE) if within the age limit. Some officers move via lateral entry to central-services deputations. Direct switching between services is rare and requires re-clearing UPSC CSE.

## Sources

- UPSC online application portal: [upsconline.nic.in](https://www.upsconline.nic.in)
- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation: [mospi.gov.in](https://www.mospi.gov.in)
- Related on this site: [UPSC CSE 2026](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-cse-2026), [SEBI Grade A 2026](/sarkari-naukri/sebi-grade-a-2026), [RBI Grade B 2026](/sarkari-naukri/rbi-grade-b-2026)

## IBPS RRB 2026: 13,706 posts, applications close 21 September

IBPS RRB 2026, formally CRP RRB XV, is the common recruitment process for Regional Rural Banks across India, conducted by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection. IBPS published the notification on 31 August 2026 for 13,706 posts, and the application window runs from 1 September to 21 September 2026 on ibps.in.

An earlier version of this page reported the notification as not yet issued, which was true when it was written on 26 August and stopped being true five days later. It also declined to repeat the vacancy figures then circulating, in the region of 3,000 to 5,000 posts. That caution was right: the published total is 13,706, roughly three times those estimates.

| Post | Vacancies |
|---|---|
| Office Assistant (Multipurpose) | 8,183 |
| Officer Scale I (Assistant Manager) | 4,256 |
| Officer Scale II (Manager) | 1,047 |
| Officer Scale III (Senior Manager) | 220 |
| **Total** | **13,706** |

Office Assistant is 60 per cent of the recruitment on its own, and it is the one post with no interview stage. The application fee is Rs 850 for general, OBC and EWS candidates, and Rs 175 for SC, ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen candidates.

Two features of RRB recruitment distinguish it from IBPS PO and IBPS Clerk, and both matter more than candidates expect. There is a local language requirement, which is a genuine eligibility gate. And the Office Assistant post has no interview stage at all, while the Officer Scale posts do.

## Confirmed exam dates

| Post | Prelims | Mains |
|---|---|---|
| Officer Scale I | 21 and 22 November 2026 | 20 December 2026 |
| Office Assistant (Multipurpose) | 6, 12 and 13 December 2026 | As per the notification |

Officer Scale II and III recruitments are conducted through a single examination rather than a prelims and mains structure, as set out in the notification for those posts.

Note the sequence. Officer Scale I prelims fall in late November, ahead of the Office Assistant prelims in December, and the Officer Scale I mains on 20 December sits between the Office Assistant prelims dates. A candidate applying for both posts, which is permitted, needs to plan for a dense five-week period rather than treating them as separate campaigns.

## The posts

| Post | Role |
|---|---|
| Office Assistant (Multipurpose) | Clerical work at branch level: counter operations, cash handling, account opening, passbook and record maintenance, customer service |
| Officer Scale I (Assistant Manager) | Entry-level officer: branch operations, credit appraisal, agricultural and rural lending, supervision of clerical staff |
| Officer Scale II (Manager) | Middle management, including specialist streams such as IT, Chartered Accountant, Law, Treasury, Marketing and Agriculture |
| Officer Scale III (Senior Manager) | Senior branch and regional responsibilities |

Regional Rural Banks operate in rural and semi-urban areas, sponsored by commercial banks and jointly owned by the central government, the sponsoring bank and the state government. The work is therefore weighted towards agricultural credit, rural deposits, government scheme disbursement, and the financial inclusion mandate, more so than at a metropolitan branch of a commercial bank.

## The local language requirement

This is the condition that most distinguishes RRB recruitment, and the one that most often disqualifies otherwise strong candidates.

Regional Rural Banks require proficiency in the local language of the state in which the bank operates. In practice this generally means having studied the local language as a subject at school level, commonly up to Class 10, and being able to read, write and speak it.

The reason is operational rather than bureaucratic. An RRB branch serves rural customers who transact in the local language, and a clerk or officer who cannot read a form filled in that language or explain a scheme to a customer cannot do the job.

Two consequences follow.

First, this is a state-linked recruitment in a way IBPS PO and Clerk are not. You apply to a specific state and bank, and your eligibility depends on the language of that state. A candidate from Bihar cannot casually apply to a Tamil Nadu RRB.

Second, candidates who studied outside their home state, or in a school where the local language was not offered, should check this carefully before applying. Verification typically happens at the document stage, which means discovering the problem after clearing two examinations.

The exact requirement is stated in the notification for each participating bank, and it is the document to check rather than a general assumption.

## Selection process, which differs by post

Candidates routinely assume a single process. There are two.

For Office Assistant (Multipurpose): a preliminary examination, then a main examination, and that is all. **There is no interview.** The final merit rests on the mains score alone.

For Officer Scale I: a preliminary examination, then a main examination, then an interview. The final merit is computed from the mains and the interview together, with the mains carrying the larger weight, commonly in an 80 to 20 ratio.

For Officer Scale II and III: a single examination followed by an interview.

That difference matters when choosing which post to apply for. A candidate who is strong on paper but finds interviews difficult has a cleaner route through Office Assistant. A candidate who interviews well has an advantage at Officer Scale I that does not exist at clerical level.

In both cases the preliminary examination is a screening stage: its marks do not carry into the final merit.

## Exam pattern

The preliminary examinations for both posts are short papers focused on reasoning and numerical ability, without a general awareness or English component.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Sections | Reasoning Ability and Numerical Ability (Quantitative Aptitude) |
| Total questions | 80 |
| Total marks | 80 |
| Duration | 45 minutes, with sectional timing |
| Negative marking | 0.25 marks per wrong answer |

The main examinations are longer, adding General Awareness with an emphasis on banking and rural economy, a language paper, and computer knowledge, for a total in the region of 200 marks. Candidates choose English or Hindi for the language paper.

Because IBPS finalises the section-wise composition of the mains in the notification, and it has varied between cycles, the structure above should be confirmed against the CRP RRB XV notification when it appears rather than assumed from a previous year.

45 minutes for 80 questions in the prelims gives you about 34 seconds per question, which makes the preliminary stage a pure speed test. Sectional timing means you cannot borrow minutes from reasoning to finish numerical ability.

## Eligibility

On age, the bands differ by post and are set in the notification, commonly running from 18 years for Office Assistant and from 18 or 21 for Officer Scale I, with upper limits in the late twenties to early thirties and the usual relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for other specified categories.

On education, a bachelor's degree in any discipline is the general requirement for both Office Assistant and Officer Scale I, with preference in some cases for candidates with degrees in agriculture, horticulture, forestry, animal husbandry, veterinary science, agricultural engineering, pisciculture, information technology, management, law, economics or accountancy. Officer Scale II specialist posts carry their own professional qualification requirements.

On language, proficiency in the local language of the state applied to, as described above.

Computer knowledge is generally required, with the notification specifying the form in which it must be evidenced.

## Salary

Office Assistant pay in Regional Rural Banks broadly tracks the clerical scale in the banking industry, and Officer Scale I broadly tracks the officer scale, both under the industry settlements applicable to RRBs.

Alongside basic pay come dearness allowance, house rent allowance depending on the classification of the branch location, transport allowance, medical benefits and pension provisions as applicable to new recruits.

One practical point specific to RRBs: because branches are in rural and semi-urban areas, house rent allowance and the cost of living are both generally lower than at a metropolitan commercial bank branch. The headline salary comparison with IBPS PO or Clerk therefore understates how far the money goes, while the posting locations are less likely to be in a large city.

Confirm the current pay scales in the notification, since banking pay is revised through periodic industry settlements.

## Career progression

Progression in an RRB runs through the officer scales.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Office Assistant | Direct entry |
| Officer Scale I | Promotion from clerical cadre, and direct recruitment |
| Officer Scale II | Promotion, and direct recruitment for specialist posts |
| Officer Scale III | Promotion |
| Senior management grades | Promotion |

An Office Assistant with a degree can move into the officer cadre through internal promotion, and many do. Alternatively, a serving clerk may sit the direct Officer Scale I recruitment in a later cycle, which is a faster route than waiting for departmental promotion.

## How IBPS RRB compares with IBPS PO and Clerk

| | IBPS RRB | [IBPS PO](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-po-2026) | [IBPS Clerk](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-clerk-2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Banks | 28 Regional Rural Banks | Public sector commercial banks | Public sector commercial banks |
| Local language | Required | Not required in the same way | Not required in the same way |
| Postings | Rural and semi-urban | All India, including metros | All India |
| Interview | Officer Scale I yes, Office Assistant no | Yes | No |

| Post | Prelims | Mains |
|---|---|---|
| Officer Scale I | 21 and 22 November 2026 | 20 December 2026 |
| Office Assistant (Multipurpose) | 6, 12 and 13 December 2026 | As per the notification |

| Officer Scale II (Manager) | Middle management, including specialist streams such as IT, Chartered Accountant, Law, Treasury, Marketing and Agriculture |
| Officer Scale III (Senior Manager) | Senior branch and regional responsibilities |

The work is therefore weighted towards agricultural credit, rural deposits, government scheme disbursement, and the financial inclusion mandate, more so than at a metropolitan branch of a commercial bank.

This is the condition that most distinguishes RRB recruitment, and the one that most often disqualifies otherwise strong candidates.

Regional Rural Banks require proficiency in the local language of the state in which the bank operates. In practice this generally means having studied the local language as a subject at school level, commonly up to Class 10, and being able to read, write and speak it.

The exact requirement is stated in the notification for each participating bank, and it is the document to check rather than a general assumption.

Candidates routinely assume a single process. There are two.

For Officer Scale I: a preliminary examination, then a main examination, then an interview. The final merit is computed from the mains and the interview together, with the mains carrying the larger weight, commonly in an 80 to 20 ratio.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Sections | Reasoning Ability and Numerical Ability (Quantitative Aptitude) |
| Total questions | 80 |
| Total marks | 80 |
| Duration | 45 minutes, with sectional timing |
| Negative marking | 0.25 marks per wrong answer |

## Junior Executive Air Traffic Control: what the role is

Air Traffic Control is the function that separates aircraft in the air and on the ground. Controllers issue clearances for takeoff, landing, routing and altitude, and they carry direct responsibility for keeping aircraft apart. AAI operates air traffic services across Indian airspace and at airports nationwide.

The work runs in shifts around the clock because airspace does not close. Controllers work rostered rotations including nights, weekends and public holidays. changes.title: MAT September 2026: CBT 20 Sep, Pattern and Cutoffs
changes.description: MAT September 2026: PBT was held 13 September, CBT is on 20 September with registration closing on the 14th. Pattern, marking and accepting institutes.
changes.content:
## MAT September 2026: the most accessible MBA entrance

MAT, the Management Aptitude Test conducted by the All India Management Association, is held four times a year. In the September 2026 session the Paper Based Test was held on 13 September 2026, its registration having closed on 7 September. The Computer Based Test is on 20 September 2026 and registration for it closes on 14 September, so only the CBT route remains open in this session.

MAT occupies a specific place in the management entrance landscape, and it is worth being straightforward about it. This is the most accessible of the major MBA entrance tests: it runs four times a year rather than once, it offers three different test modes, its eligibility conditions are the lightest, and its score is accepted by a very large number of institutes.

What it is not is a route to the IIMs, which use CAT. Candidates targeting the top tier should sit CAT and treat MAT as a parallel option rather than a substitute. Candidates targeting the broad middle of Indian management education, where several hundred institutes accept MAT, will find it the most practical test on the calendar.

That framing matters because it determines whether MAT is the right use of your September.

## Important dates for the September 2026 session

| Mode | Registration closes | Exam date |
|---|---|---|
| Paper Based Test (PBT) | 7 September 2026 | 13 September 2026 |
| Computer Based Test (CBT) | 14 September 2026 | 20 September 2026 |
| Internet Based Test (IBT) | As announced by AIMA | Announced separately after registration opens |

AIMA announces IBT dates for each session separately, so candidates preferring that mode should watch the official portal rather than assume a date.

Note how short the runway is between closing and sitting. PBT registration closed on 7 September and the exam followed six days later, on the 13th. The CBT repeats that pattern: registration closes on 14 September for an exam on the 20th, with the admit card released on 17 September. Six days is not enough to start preparing, which is the practical argument for deciding on a MAT session well before its deadline.

## The three test modes

MAT is the only major Indian management entrance test offering a genuine choice of delivery mode, and the differences are practical rather than academic.

The Paper Based Test is a conventional pen and paper examination at a designated centre, with the question paper and OMR sheet. It suits candidates who prefer reading on paper and marking answers physically, and who are comfortable travelling to a centre.

The Computer Based Test is taken on a computer at a designated centre, in the same format as most other entrance examinations. It suits candidates already practised on screen.

The Internet Based Test is taken remotely with proctoring, meaning you sit the examination from home or another approved location under remote supervision. It removes travel entirely, which matters for candidates in smaller towns without a nearby centre, but requires a stable internet connection, a working webcam and an environment that satisfies the proctoring conditions.

You may also sit more than one format in the same session. The fee is Rs 2,300 for a single format and Rs 4,000 for both, which works out cheaper than two separate registrations and gives you a second attempt within the same cycle.

## Exam pattern

MAT is a test of 150 multiple choice questions in 120 minutes, across five equally sized sections.

| Section | Questions |
|---|---|
| Language Comprehension | 30 |
| Intelligence and Critical Reasoning | 30 |
| Data Analysis and Data Sufficiency | 30 |
| Mathematical Skills | 30 |
| Economic and Business Environment | 30 |
| Total | 150 |

Marking is straightforward: 1 mark for a correct answer, 0.25 deducted for a wrong answer, and nothing for an unattempted question. The composite result is reported on a scaled range running up to 800.

At 150 questions in 120 minutes you have 48 seconds per question, which places MAT among the faster papers on the circuit despite its individual questions being generally more direct than CAT's.

## The section no other MBA entrance has

Economic and Business Environment is worth singling out, because nothing in CAT, XAT, SNAP or NMAT prepares you for it.

It tests awareness of the economy and the business world: economic concepts and indicators, government economic policy and budget provisions, banking and financial institutions, company and brand awareness, business personalities, mergers and acquisitions, international trade and organisations, and current business affairs.

For a candidate preparing across several entrance tests, this is the one MAT-specific investment required. The good news is that it is a knowledge section rather than an aptitude one, which means it responds directly to study in a way that reasoning ability does not. A few weeks of reading business news and revising basic economics converts reliably into marks.

Candidates should check the weighting their target institutes apply, since institutes differ in how they treat the sections when computing their own cutoffs.

## Negative marking and attempt strategy

The penalty is 0.25 against 1 mark for a correct answer, the same 4 to 1 ratio SNAP uses.

Working the arithmetic: a blind guess among four options yields on average one correct at plus 1 and three wrong at minus 0.75, a net positive of 0.25. So guessing carries a small positive expected value even with no elimination, and eliminating a single option makes attempting clearly worthwhile.

On a 150-question paper the practical implication is that you should finish with very few blanks. Candidates who leave thirty questions unattempted out of caution are discarding marks that the marking scheme is offering them.

There is no sectional time limit, so the 120 minutes may be distributed across the five sections as you choose. As with SNAP, that freedom helps prepared candidates and hurts unprepared ones, since nothing forces you out of a section you are stuck in.

## Eligibility

A bachelor's degree from a recognised institution in any discipline is required.

Final-year students are eligible to apply.

MAT does not impose a minimum percentage requirement or an age limit at the test level, which makes it the lightest eligibility bar among the major management entrance examinations. Individual institutes set their own admission conditions, so check those for your target colleges.

That openness is a genuine advantage for candidates whose graduation marks fall below the 50 per cent floor that CAT and SNAP apply.

## Which institutes accept MAT

Several hundred management institutes across India accept the MAT score, spanning university departments, autonomous institutes and private business schools. AIMA publishes a list of participating institutes for each session.

The IIMs do not accept MAT. Nor do most of the top-tier institutes that use CAT or their own tests. What MAT opens is the broad middle and regional tier of Indian management education, which is a large and legitimate segment but a different one.

Because acceptance is wide and cutoffs vary enormously between institutes, the practical work after the result is researching which participating institutes match your score and your location preferences, then applying to each separately. As with the other entrance tests, the score generates eligibility rather than admission, and institutes run their own group discussion and interview rounds.

## How MAT compares with the other management entrance exams

| Exam | Frequency | Questions and time | Negative marking | Accepted by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [CAT 2026](/entrance-exams/cat-2026) | Once a year | 68 in 120 min | Yes, on MCQs | IIMs and several hundred others |
| [XAT 2027](/entrance-exams/xat-2027) | Once a year | 95 in 180 min | Yes, plus blank penalty | XLRI and 250+ others |
| [SNAP 2026](/entrance-exams/snap-2026) | Once a year, three dates | 60 in 60 min | Yes, 0.25 | Symbiosis institutes |
| [NMAT 2026](/entrance-exams/nmat-2026) | Once a year, 70-day window | 108 in 120 min | None | NMIMS and others |
| MAT September 2026 | Four times a year | 150 in 120 min | Yes, 0.25 | Several hundred institutes, not the IIMs |

The frequency is MAT's defining advantage. Four sessions a year means a candidate who is not ready in September can sit in December, and one who underperforms can retake within months rather than waiting a full year. For candidates working, or preparing alongside other commitments, that flexibility is worth a great deal.

## Preparing for MAT

Prioritise Economic and Business Environment if you are preparing for several tests, since it is the only genuinely MAT-specific content and it responds directly to study.

Practise at pace. At 48 seconds per question the paper rewards quick, accurate work on moderate questions rather than deep problem solving, and a candidate who is accurate but slow will leave more marks unclaimed than one who is fast and occasionally wrong.

Use the absence of sectional limits deliberately by deciding in advance roughly how long each section gets, and stick to it. The common failure on papers without locks is over-investing in one section.

Attempt nearly everything, given the positive expected value of guessing under a 4 to 1 penalty ratio.

Take timed 150-question mocks in your chosen mode. If you have selected the Internet Based Test, practise on screen at home under conditions resembling the proctored environment, since the setup itself is unfamiliar to most candidates.

Consider registering for both formats at Rs 4,000. Two attempts within one session, at less than the cost of two separate registrations, is good value if you can spare the second date.

Work Data Analysis and Data Sufficiency deliberately, since it and Mathematical Skills together account for 60 of the 150 questions. Data sufficiency in particular is a question type many candidates meet for the first time in MAT, and it rewards recognising when the given information settles the question rather than actually solving it, which is a distinct habit worth drilling separately.

## Choosing which mode to sit

The three modes are not equivalent in practice, and the choice deserves a moment's thought rather than defaulting to whichever deadline is furthest away.

Take the Paper Based Test if you read faster on paper, if you like being able to flip back through a physical booklet, and if you have a centre within comfortable travelling distance. Its deadline is the earliest of the three, on 7 September.

Take the Computer Based Test if you are already practised on screen from other entrance tests, since the interface will feel familiar and the marking and review tools work the way you expect. Its deadline of 14 September gives you an extra week to decide.

Take the Internet Based Test if travel is the binding constraint. Sitting from home removes the journey and the unfamiliar centre entirely, which for candidates in smaller towns can be the difference between attempting and not attempting. The trade-offs are real, though: you need a stable connection for the full two hours, a working webcam, and a room that satisfies the proctoring rules on lighting, noise and the absence of other people. A connection failure mid-test is a genuinely stressful situation, so this mode suits candidates confident in their setup.

If you can spare two dates, registering for two formats at Rs 4,000 sidesteps the decision entirely and gives you a second attempt in the same session.

## What happens after the result

MAT results are published on the AIMA portal along with a scorecard reporting your composite score and sectional performance.

From there, the work is yours. AIMA sends your score to the institutes you nominated during registration, but each institute runs its own admission process with its own cutoff, application form and selection round. Because MAT is accepted by several hundred institutes with cutoffs varying enormously, the practical task after the result is matching your score against participating institutes in the locations you would actually attend, then applying to each separately.

Selection rounds at MAT-accepting institutes typically involve a group discussion and a personal interview, with some institutes adding a written assessment. Weightage formulas differ, and many give explicit weight to academic record and work experience alongside the test score.

Candidates who treat the score as the finish line lose time here. Research your target institutes while waiting for the result rather than after it, since application windows at several of them close quickly once scores are out.

## How to apply

Registration is on the official AIMA MAT portal at mat.aima.in.

1. Register with a valid email address and mobile number, used for the admit card and all communication.
2. Complete the application with academic details exactly as on your certificates.
3. Choose your test mode: Paper Based Test, Computer Based Test, Internet Based Test, or two formats together.
4. Select your test centre and city preferences where the mode requires it.
5. Select the management institutes to which your score should be sent, as provided in the application.
6. Pay the fee: Rs 2,300 for one format or Rs 4,000 for two.
7. Submit and save the confirmation, then download the admit card when released ahead of your exam date.

Watch the deadlines carefully, since they differ by mode: 7 September for the paper based test and 14 September for the computer based test.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 and Class 12 mark sheets and certificates.
2. Graduation mark sheets and degree certificate, or evidence of final-year enrolment.
3. A valid photo identity document matching your registration.
4. Category certificate where a target institute applies reservation.
5. Photograph and signature in the specified format.
6. For the Internet Based Test, a computer with a working webcam, a stable internet connection and a room that meets the proctoring requirements.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is MAT September 2026 and when does registration close?**
The Paper Based Test is on 13 September 2026 with registration closing on 7 September, and the Computer Based Test is on 20 September 2026 with registration closing on 14 September. Internet Based Test dates are announced separately by AIMA after registration opens. The deadlines differ by mode, so check the one that applies to your chosen format.

**What is the MAT exam pattern?**
150 multiple choice questions in 120 minutes across five equally sized sections of 30 questions each: Language Comprehension, Intelligence and Critical Reasoning, Data Analysis and Data Sufficiency, Mathematical Skills, and Economic and Business Environment. Marking is +1 for a correct answer and -0.25 for a wrong one, with nothing deducted for unattempted questions, and the composite result is reported on a scale up to 800.

**Is there negative marking in MAT?**
Yes, 0.25 marks for each wrong answer against 1 mark for a correct one. That 4 to 1 ratio means a blind guess among four options carries a small positive expected value, so very few questions should be left blank on a 150-question paper. Unattempted questions score zero with no penalty.

**How many times a year is MAT conducted?**
Four times, which is MAT's defining advantage over the other management entrance tests that run once a year. A candidate who is not ready for the September session can sit in December, and one who underperforms can retake within months rather than waiting a full year.

**What are the three MAT test modes?**
Paper Based Test at a centre using a question paper and OMR sheet; Computer Based Test at a centre; and Internet Based Test taken remotely under proctoring from home or another approved location. The IBT removes travel entirely, which helps candidates without a nearby centre, but needs a stable connection, a webcam and an environment meeting the proctoring conditions. You may sit two formats in the same session.

**What is the MAT registration fee?**
Rs 2,300 for a single format and Rs 4,000 for two formats together, which is cheaper than two separate registrations and gives you a second attempt within the same session.

**Do the IIMs accept MAT scores?**
No. The IIMs use CAT. MAT is accepted by several hundred other management institutes across university departments, autonomous institutes and private business schools, covering the broad middle and regional tier of Indian management education. Candidates targeting the top tier should sit CAT and treat MAT as a parallel option rather than a substitute.

**What is the Economic and Business Environment section in MAT?**
A 30-question section unique to MAT among the major entrance tests, covering economic concepts and indicators, government economic policy and budget provisions, banking and financial institutions, company and brand awareness, business personalities, mergers and acquisitions, international trade and current business affairs. Since it is a knowledge section rather than an aptitude one, it responds directly to a few weeks of reading business news and revising basic economics.

**What is the eligibility for MAT?**
A bachelor's degree from a recognised institution in any discipline, with final-year students also eligible. MAT sets no minimum percentage requirement and no age limit at test level, making it the lightest eligibility bar among the major management entrance examinations. Individual institutes set their own admission conditions.

**Does MAT have sectional time limits?**
No. The full 120 minutes may be distributed across the five sections as you choose, and you may move between them freely. As with SNAP, that freedom helps prepared candidates and hurts unprepared ones, so decide your rough time allocation per section in advance rather than during the paper.

**Should I take MAT if I am preparing for CAT?**
It depends on your target institutes. If you are aiming at the IIMs and top-tier schools, CAT is the necessary test and MAT adds options in the broader tier rather than at the top. If your realistic target set includes institutes that accept MAT, sitting it is worthwhile since the syllabus overlaps substantially and the only genuinely new content is the Economic and Business Environment section.

**Can I take MAT more than once in a session?**
Yes. Registering for two formats at Rs 4,000 gives you two attempts within the same September session, at less than the cost of two separate registrations. Beyond that, MAT runs four sessions a year, so further attempts are available in December and in the following February and May sessions.

| [XAT 2027](/entrance-exams/xat-2027) | Once a year | 95 in 180 min | Yes, plus blank penalty | XLRI and 250+ others |
| [SNAP 2026](/entrance-exams/snap-2026) | Once a year, three dates | 60 in 60 min | Yes, 0.25 | Symbiosis institutes |
| [NMAT 2026](/entrance-exams/nmat-2026) | Once a year, 70-day window | 108 in 120 min | None | NMIMS and others |
| MAT September 2026 | Four times a year | 150 in 120 min | Yes, 0.25 | Several hundred institutes, not the IIMs |

The frequency is MAT's defining advantage. Four sessions a year means a candidate who is not ready in September can sit in December, and one who underperforms can retake within months rather than waiting a full year. For candidates working, or preparing alongside other commitments, that flexibility is worth a great deal.

## Preparing for MAT

Prioritise Economic and Business Environment if you are preparing for several tests, since it is the only genuinely MAT-specific content and it responds directly to study.

Practise at pace. At 48 seconds per question the paper rewards quick, accurate work on moderate questions rather than deep problem solving, and a candidate who is accurate but slow will leave more marks unclaimed than one who is fast and occasionally wrong.

Use the absence of sectional limits deliberately by deciding in advance roughly how long each section gets, and stick to it. The common failure on papers without locks is over-investing in one section.

Attempt nearly everything, given the positive expected value of guessing under a 4 to 1 penalty ratio.

Take timed 150-question mocks in your chosen mode. If you have selected the Internet Based Test, practise on screen at home under conditions resembling the proctored environment, since the setup itself is unfamiliar to most candidates.

Consider registering for both formats at Rs 4,000. Two attempts within one session, at less than the cost of two separate registrations, is good value if you can spare the second date.

Work Data Analysis and Data Sufficiency deliberately, since it and Mathematical Skills together account for 60 of the 150 questions. Data sufficiency in particular is a question type many candidates meet for the first time in MAT, and it rewards recognising when the given information settles the question rather than actually solving it, which is a distinct habit worth drilling separately.

## Choosing which mode to sit

The three modes are not equivalent in practice, and the choice deserves a moment's thought rather than defaulting to whichever deadline is furthest away.

Take the Paper Based Test if you read faster on paper, if you like being able to flip back through a physical booklet, and if you have a centre within comfortable travelling distance. Its deadline is the earliest of the three, on 7 September.

Take the Computer Based Test if you are already practised on screen from other entrance tests, since the interface will feel familiar and the marking and review tools work the way you expect. Its deadline of 14 September gives you an extra week to decide.

Take the Internet Based Test if travel is the binding constraint. Sitting from home removes the journey and the unfamiliar centre entirely, which for candidates in smaller towns can be the difference between attempting and not attempting. The trade-offs are real, though: you need a stable connection for the full two hours, a working webcam, and a room that satisfies the proctoring rules on lighting, noise and the absence of other people. A connection failure mid-test is a genuinely stressful situation, so this mode suits candidates confident in their setup.

If you can spare two dates, registering for two formats at Rs 4,000 sidesteps the decision entirely and gives you a second attempt in the same session.

## What happens after the result

MAT results are published on the AIMA portal along with a scorecard reporting your composite score and sectional performance.

From there, the work is yours. AIMA sends your score to the institutes you nominated during registration, but each institute runs its own admission process with its own cutoff, application form and selection round. Because MAT is accepted by several hundred institutes with cutoffs varying enormously, the practical task after the result is matching your score against participating institutes in the locations you would actually attend, then applying to each separately.

Selection rounds at MAT-accepting institutes typically involve a group discussion and a personal interview, with some institutes adding a written assessment. Weightage formulas differ, and many give explicit weight to academic record and work experience alongside the test score.

Candidates who treat the score as the finish line lose time here. Research your target institutes while waiting for the result rather than after it, since application windows at several of them close quickly once scores are out.

## How to apply

Registration is on the official AIMA MAT portal at mat.aima.in.

1. Register with a valid email address and mobile number, used for the admit card and all communication.
2. Complete the application with academic details exactly as on your certificates.
3. Choose your test mode: Paper Based Test, Computer Based Test, Internet Based Test, or two formats together.
4. Select your test centre and city preferences where the mode requires it.
5. Select the management institutes to which your score should be sent, as provided in the application.
6. Pay the fee: Rs 2,300 for one format or Rs 4,000 for two.
7. Submit and save the confirmation, then download the admit card when released ahead of your exam date.

Watch the deadlines carefully, since they differ by mode: 7 September for the paper based test and 14 September for the computer based test.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 and Class 12 mark sheets and certificates.
2. Graduation mark sheets and degree certificate, or evidence of final-year enrolment.
3. A valid photo identity document matching your registration.
4. Category certificate where a target institute applies reservation.
5. Photograph and signature in the specified format.
6. For the Internet Based Test, a computer with a working webcam, a stable internet connection and a room that meets the proctoring requirements.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is MAT September 2026 and when does registration close?**
The Paper Based Test is on 13 September 2026 with registration closing on 7 September, and the Computer Based Test is on 20 September 2026 with registration closing on 14 September. Internet Based Test dates are announced separately by AIMA after registration opens. The deadlines differ by mode, so check the one that applies to your chosen format.

**What is the MAT exam pattern?**
150 multiple choice questions in 120 minutes across five equally sized sections of 30 questions each: Language Comprehension, Intelligence and Critical Reasoning, Data Analysis and Data Sufficiency, Mathematical Skills, and Economic and Business Environment. Marking is +1 for a correct answer and -0.25 for a wrong one, with nothing deducted for unattempted questions, and the composite result is reported on a scale up to 800.

**Is there negative marking in MAT?**
Yes, 0.25 marks for each wrong answer against 1 mark for a correct one. That 4 to 1 ratio means a blind guess among four options carries a small positive expected value, so very few questions should be left blank on a 150-question paper. Unattempted questions score zero with no penalty.

**How many times a year is MAT conducted?**
Four times, which is MAT's defining advantage over the other management entrance tests that run once a year. A candidate who is not ready for the September session can sit in December, and one who underperforms can retake within months rather than waiting a full year.

**What are the three MAT test modes?**
Paper Based Test at a centre using a question paper and OMR sheet; Computer Based Test at a centre; and Internet Based Test taken remotely under proctoring from home or another approved location. The IBT removes travel entirely, which helps candidates without a nearby centre, but needs a stable connection, a webcam and an environment meeting the proctoring conditions. You may sit two formats in the same session.

**What is the MAT registration fee?**
Rs 2,300 for a single format and Rs 4,000 for two formats together, which is cheaper than two separate registrations and gives you a second attempt within the same session.

**Do the IIMs accept MAT scores?**
No. The IIMs use CAT. MAT is accepted by several hundred other management institutes across university departments, autonomous institutes and private business schools, covering the broad middle and regional tier of Indian management education. Candidates targeting the top tier should sit CAT and treat MAT as a parallel option rather than a substitute.

**What is the Economic and Business Environment section in MAT?**
A 30-question section unique to MAT among the major entrance tests, covering economic concepts and indicators, government economic policy and budget provisions, banking and financial institutions, company and brand awareness, business personalities, mergers and acquisitions, international trade and current business affairs. Since it is a knowledge section rather than an aptitude one, it responds directly to a few weeks of reading business news and revising basic economics.

**What is the eligibility for MAT?**
A bachelor's degree from a recognised institution in any discipline, with final-year students also eligible. MAT sets no minimum percentage requirement and no age limit at test level, making it the lightest eligibility bar among the major management entrance examinations. Individual institutes set their own admission conditions.

**Does MAT have sectional time limits?**
No. The full 120 minutes may be distributed across the five sections as you choose, and you may move between them freely. As with SNAP, that freedom helps prepared candidates and hurts unprepared ones, so decide your rough time allocation per section in advance rather than during the paper.

**Should I take MAT if I am preparing for CAT?**
It depends on your target institutes. If you are aiming at the IIMs and top-tier schools, CAT is the necessary test and MAT adds options in the broader tier rather than at the top. If your realistic target set includes institutes that accept MAT, sitting it is worthwhile since the syllabus overlaps substantially and the only genuinely new content is the Economic and Business Environment section.

**Can I take MAT more than once in a session?**
Yes. Registering for two formats at Rs 4,000 gives you two attempts within the same September session, at less than the cost of two separate registrations. Beyond that, MAT runs four sessions a year, so further attempts are available in December and in the following February and May sessions.
